newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity flows to US stock funds positive in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity flows to US stock funds positive in Oct.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Wednesday net sales for its U.S. stock mutual funds in October were "slightly positive" despite moderate net sales of the funds across the industry.

"Our equity sales slowed down quite a bit from September," Fidelity spokeswoman Robyn Tice said. "The market set a new record and crossed the 6,000 threshold and we think some investors may have taken some profits."

International equities had an estimated cash outflow of more than $100 million for the month, bond funds also lost more than an estimated $100 million and money market funds had net cash inflows of more than an estimated $3 billion.
Analysts said weak returns at many of Fidelity's equity funds has caused the company to lose market share.
"Their market share is down to one or two percent," down from 18 to 20 percent at the beginning of the year, said David O'Leary, president of Alpha Equity Research of Portsmouth, New Hampshire.
O'Leary estimates that investors have pulled out $3.8 billion from Fidelity's flagship Magellan Fund since the beginning of the year and more than $1 billion in October alone.
"October so far is the worst month of the year. The Magellan impact is growing every month," he said.

Tice declined to discuss market share. However she said Fidelity's share of total mutual fund assets has grown consistently over the past few years, and its assets earmarked for 401K retirement plans are expected to have a record year.
The Investment Company Institute, an industry body, said Wednesday new cash flows into U.S. stock mutual funds dropped to an estimated $13 billion in October.
Net sales of domestic equity mutual funds were down from $17.4 billion in September, and have been declining since May, the ICI said.
